explanation: L13/H7 is a running nominal-copy head with a text-start baseline: at the finite verb, auxiliary or following function word it attends one preceding token, normally a nominal - the clause's subject (a determiner+noun, a role or person noun, a proper name, or a subject pronoun such as us/them/anyone/nobody/everyone), one to four tokens back, skipping a verb or preposition to reach it - and writes that token's value minus its own mean write, which is close to the value of the text's first position, so its strength is the share of attention on that nominal times that nominal's value distance, and that distance grows with how far into the text the nominal sits. Hence a later clause's subject normally crosses the line once it sits four or more tokens into the text (a second subject after 'and' or a comma: the bank closed 2.7, the committee approved 3.0, the girl checked 2.7, the judge signed 4.2, the technician logged 3.2 when the first clause is 'the clerk read the note' but only 1.7 after 'the chemist weighed the sample', so the lock is graded, not categorical), as do most role, person and proper-name subjects at their verb in an opening clause (the judge signed 2.7, the clerk filed 2.9, the waiter handed 4.4) and subject pronouns at their verb when they are not the text's first token (nobody 3.1, anyone 2.7, us 5.0), while an opening clause with an institutional or collective subject stays under the line (the council approved 0.4-0.9, the committee reviewed 1.2, the bank closed 1.6, the train arrived 0.3), and agentless passive clauses and expletive or predicate frames retrieve no nominal and sit at the floor (a decision was reached -0.3, the report was submitted 1.2, the readings were recorded 0.4, it was fine -1.1, they said it was fine -0.4); ordinary multi-clause prose therefore crosses somewhere and is active-weak.
